Ruling

Partial refund PARTIAL_REFUND

Refund to the rider: SGD 5.00

The judge's explanation, as written

To the rider: you are entitled to a partial refund of SGD 5.00, and the reasons are set out below so you can check the arithmetic. To the driver: the deviation on this trip is measured, not alleged, and it is not excused. Distance and deviation. The fare_breakdown shows a METERED fare, so the distance figure that governs is the GPS trace, not the rounded copy on the trip record: trace_distance_km 20.28 km (EV-GPS-02832) against the booked optimal 15.6 km (EV-TRIP-02832). That is an excess of 4.68 km, or 30.0%, which passes both establishment gates of POL-RD-01 (>20% and >0.8 km) and clears neither materiality gate (>50% and >8.0 km). Fare recomputation under POL-RD-02. Surge was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (EV-FARE-02832) and is 1.0. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 15.6 km + 0.28 x 21.1 min) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 22.2080. Charged_total was 27.19; refund = 27.19 - 22.2080 = 4.9820, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and only 18.3% of the charge, so it stays a partial refund and rounds UP to SGD 5.00. The three figures are: charged_total 27.19, recomputed_fare 22.2080, refund payable 5.00. You asked for 5.50; the arithmetic supports 5.00, because the refund is the difference between what you paid and what the optimal route would have cost. Why no clause reduces or enlarges that figure. The chat instruction 'stop at IMM first please' is genuine, rider-sent and timely, but the trace never brought the vehicle within 200 m of the hinted waypoint - the nearest fix was 1677.44 m away - so POL-RD-04 corroboration fails, no distance is excluded, and under POL-RD-14 this is a failed reliance rather than the contradiction that would escalate under POL-RD-10(7). No traffic advisory exists on file (EV-ADVIS-02832-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0), so POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing. No ERP, toll, airport surcharge or waiting-time line exists, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing on top and nothing is double-counted. The deviation is not material and the driver's 90-day counters show no pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 of 328 completed trips), so no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral arises. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes too (159 fixes, 10 s interval, no gaps), so no POL-RD-07 or POL-RD-10 issue is present. Profile fields such as rating, account age and lifetime counters were not used as grounds - they are context only under POL-GEN-01. No referral is produced by any clause on these facts. The monetary effect (5.00) is within the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so the refund issues automatically; this remains a provisional ruling and either party may appeal it once under POL-GEN-04. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

How to appeal: Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

What each side argued

The rider advocate

kept The deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The GPS polyline measures 20.28 km against a booked optimal of 15.6 km, an excess of 4.68 km — 30.0% of optimal. Both limbs of the POL-RD-01 test pass: the excess exceeds 20% of optimal (3.12 km) and exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms. Nothing more is needed for establishment, and the excess remains at the measured figure because no adjustment clause applies (see the waypoint claim below).

evidence EV-GPS-02832, EV-TRIP-02832 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept The governing distance figure is the trace figure, not the rounded convenience copy. POL-RD-01 provides expressly that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km (20.28 km) and trip_record.actual_distance_km (20.3 km) disagree, the trace governs and the trip_record figure may NOT be cited for the threshold test. The excess is therefore 20.28 - 15.6 = 4.68 km, and on either figure the 30% excess is far outside the 20% / 0.8 km gate.

evidence EV-GPS-02832, EV-TRIP-02832 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. All three artifacts describe the same trip: trip_record EV-TRIP-02832, gps_trace EV-GPS-02832 and fare_breakdown EV-FARE-02832 all carry trip_id TRP-02832, and the timestamps are consistent rather than contradictory — the trace's first fix (15:17:42) matches the recorded meter start, and the fare was charged at 15:44:27 on the same afternoon. The trace is not impaired (see the integrity claim), so no independent-source substitution is required, and the rider's own 60-day counter (rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d = 0) means the extra-corroboration condition in the final sentence of POL-RD-08 is not triggered either.

evidence EV-TRIP-02832, EV-GPS-02832, EV-FARE-02832, EV-RPROF-02832 · clauses POL-RD-08

kept The chat instruction 'stop at IMM first please' does NOT exonerate any of the measured excess, and the trace proves it. The rider's message carries waypoint_hint IMM (1.3348, 103.7466), but the closest the vehicle ever came to that waypoint was 1677.44 m, at fix index 78 (15:30:42) — more than eight times the 200 m corroboration radius POL-RD-04 requires, and the derived waypoint test records within_threshold = false. Under POL-RD-04 the corroboration test therefore fails, and under POL-RD-14 that failure is a failed corroboration and not a POL-RD-10(7) contradiction: a request that was made and a route that did not follow it are consistent with each other. The consequence is that POL-RD-04 is unavailable, no distance is excluded, and the deviation is decided under POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 on the trace as measured.

evidence EV-CHAT-02832, EV-GPS-02832 · clauses POL-RD-04, POL-RD-14

kept The driver's counterparty statement — 'The rider asked for IMM, it is in the chat' — is exactly the kind of bare assertion POL-RD-08 says does not discharge the driver's burden. The burden shifted to the driver once the rider showed a threshold excess, and the driver must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause. He does not: POL-RD-03 fails for want of any advisory (next claim), POL-RD-04 fails because the vehicle never within 200 m of the waypoint it names, and nothing in the record supports POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12 (the trip is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and no amended optimal distance exists). The excess therefore stands unreduced.

evidence EV-CHAT-02832, EV-GPS-02832, EV-TRIP-02832 · clauses POL-RD-08, POL-RD-14

kept There is no traffic advisory on file that could exonerate the driver, and I disclose the impairment of the artifact I rely on for that absence: EV-ADVIS-02832-01 has admissibility status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, with the assessor's detail 'No advisory covers the Blk 55 Lengkok Bahru corridor in this window.' A MISSING artifact can carry no fact but its absence is itself citable. No advisory names a road or segment the optimal route traverses, so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and any external-cause explanation carries no weight under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08.

evidence EV-ADVIS-02832-01, EV-TRIP-02832 · clauses POL-RD-03, POL-RD-13

kept The refund is arithmetic, and it should be issued rather than anything larger or smaller. This is a METERED fare on the fare_breakdown, so POL-RD-02 governs: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 15.6 + 0.28 x 21.1) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharge + 0 waiting time - 0 promo = 22.2080. Charged_total was 27.19. Refund = 27.19 - 22.2080 = 4.9820, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is only 18.3% of charged_total — far short of the 90% full-refund share. Rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 the amount payable is SGD 5.00, and the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. The three figures should be stated on separate lines: charged_total 27.19, recomputed_fare 22.2080, refund 5.00.

evidence EV-FARE-02832, EV-TRIP-02832 · clauses POL-RD-02

evidence EV-FARE-02832 · clauses POL-RD-09

None of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met — no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 s — so the deviation stands on the trace without independent corroboration and POL-RD-10(3) does not fire.

evidence EV-GPS-02832 · clauses POL-RD-07, POL-RD-10

The case is decidable, and the disputed amount should be refunded rather than held.

evidence EV-TRIP-02832, EV-GPS-02832, EV-FARE-02832 · clauses POL-RD-10, POL-RD-14

kept For completeness and to be candid about the remedy ceiling: the rider does not seek a POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern uplift, because none is available. The excess here is 30.0% and 4.68 km, short of the 50% / 8.0 km materiality marks, and the driver's records — driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d 328 — establish no pattern under either limb of the POL-RD-06 test. The remedy is therefore the ordinary POL-RD-02 partial refund and nothing beyond it.

evidence EV-DPROF-02832, EV-TRIP-02832 · clauses POL-RD-06, POL-GEN-01

The driver advocate

kept MSG-02832-001 in the trip's own chat log is the rider's message, sent at 15:18:42 — exactly 60 seconds after the meter started at 15:17:42 — reading 'stop at IMM first please' and carrying a resolved waypoint_hint of IMM at 1.3348, 103.7466; the driver answered 'ok' 15 seconds later. That instruction is rider-sent, timely and specific enough to act on, so POL-RD-04 limbs (a) to (c) are met. What fails is the corroboration limb: the trace's nearest fix to the hinted waypoint is 1,677.4 m away, so the vehicle never came within the 200 m radius, and the driver does not ask the Judge to exclude any distance on the strength of it. Under POL-RD-14 an instruction that the trace does not corroborate in that sense is a reliance that fails on the trace, not the partly-corroborated contradiction that engages POL-RD-10(7), so the case is decided on the trace as measured. The rider's assertion that the driver 'just drove around' is only half the picture: the request came from the rider in writing one minute into the trip, and the trace shows the vehicle coming to within about 1.7 km of the stop the rider named before it went on to the booked drop-off at Blk 610 Clementi West St 1.

evidence EV-CHAT-02832, EV-GPS-02832 · clauses POL-RD-04, POL-RD-14

kept The deviation is established, and it is bounded. The trace distance of 20.28 km against the booked optimal of 15.6 km gives an excess of 4.68 km and of 30.0% — above the POL-RD-01 establishment gate of 0.8 km and 20%, but below BOTH materiality gates of 8.0 km and 50% — and the trace figure governs, so the rounded trip_record copy of 20.3 km may not be cited for the threshold test. The driver does not dispute that a deviation is established, and no exculpatory clause rescues it on this record, so the driver's case is not that the excess disappears but that the consequences are confined to the POL-RD-02 arithmetic and are not enlarged by materiality, uplift, referral or pass-through corrections.

evidence EV-GPS-02832, EV-TRIP-02832 · clauses POL-RD-01

kept The refund works out to SGD 5.00, not the SGD 5.50 contested. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 15.6 + 0.28 x 21.1) x surge_multiplier 1.0 read off the fare_breakdown + 0.80 platform fee = 22.2080; charged_total is 27.19; the refund is 4.9820, above the 0.50 de minimis so NO_ACTION is unavailable, but only 18.3% of charged_total and therefore far short of the 90% that would convert it to a FULL_REFUND, and it rounds UP to SGD 5.00 payable. The rider's claim is overstated by 0.50 and the award on this trip can be no higher than 5.00.

evidence EV-FARE-02832, EV-TRIP-02832 · clauses POL-RD-02, POL-RD-11

kept No uplift and no conduct referral can attach to this trip. POL-RD-06 is not engaged at all, because the excess of 4.68 km and 30.0% clears neither materiality gate, and even on the clause's own forward-looking fields no pattern exists: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 328, which is neither 3 or more flags nor a ratio of 0.05 or more. Those two fields are the only driver_profile fields POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 permit to be used for this test; the driver's rating, lifetime counters, cancellation rate and acceptance rate are context only and ground nothing. So no FULL_REFUND under POL-RD-06(b) and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) arise here.

evidence EV-DPROF-02832, EV-GPS-02832 · clauses POL-RD-06, POL-GEN-01

kept Nothing may be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries at all (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00, both the on-route and off-route ERP totals 0.00), no airport surcharge line (0.00) and no waiting-time fee (0.00), so there is no independent pass-through correction to stack on the distance refund; POL-RD-09(1) forbids exactly that stacking, because off-route ERP is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 recomputation. The rider's recovery is therefore the single figure of 5.00 and nothing else.

evidence EV-FARE-02832, EV-TRIP-02832 · clauses POL-RD-09, POL-RD-02

kept There is no billing-integrity defect for the rider to recover separately. The rider was billed 20.3 km against a trace of 20.28 km, so the meter tracked the distance actually driven and every charge line has its counterpart in the trace — this is a complaint about the route taken, not about being charged for distance that was never driven. No phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge exists, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to repair and no charge line stands unmatched.

To both parties: this is a real but ordinary route deviation, and the arithmetic settles it. THE DEVIATION AND ITS SIZE. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02832) measures the route actually driven at 20.28 km against the booked optimal of 15.6 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02832) — an excess of 4.68 km, or 30.0% of optimal. That clears both limbs of the POL-RD-01 establishment test (more than 0.8 km, and more than 20% of optimal), so a deviation is established. The trace figure governs; the rounded 20.3 km copy on the trip record may not be used for the threshold test. The excess reaches neither materiality mark (50% / 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged: no repeat-pattern uplift and no driver-conduct referral arise — and independently, the driver's 90-day counters (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 328 completed trips) show no pattern. THE IMM REQUEST. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02832) shows the rider wrote 'stop at IMM first please' at 15:18:42, one minute after the meter started, with a resolved waypoint, and the driver answered 'ok'. Under POL-RD-04 that instruction had to be corroborated by the trace passing within 200 m of the waypoint. It never did: the nearest fix was 1,677.4 m away. POL-RD-14 governs — a request that was made and a route that did not follow it are consistent with each other, so this is a failed corroboration, not the comparable-strength contradiction POL-RD-10(7) describes. No distance is excluded, and no escalation follows. The same failure disposes of the driver's statement that 'the rider asked for IMM': the request is on the record, but it does not account for the distance driven. OTHER EXCUSES. There is no traffic advisory on file for this window (EV-ADVIS-02832-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and no external-cause explanation carries weight. No pickup or dropoff amendment was made, and the trip is RYDE_X rather than a pooled trip, so POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 do not apply. No rider-requested-detour compensation arises either: the rider was billed 20.3 km, not less than the 20.28 km trace. THE MONEY — three figures on separate lines. Charged_total (EV-FARE-02832): 27.19. Recomputed fare under POL-RD-02: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 15.6 + 0.28 x 21.1) x 1.0 surge, read from the fare breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee = 22.2080. Refund: 27.19 - 22.2080 = 4.9820, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 5.00. That is above the 0.50 de minimis and only 18.3% of the charged total, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND — not a full refund, and not no action. Nothing is added on top: the fare carries no ERP lines, no airport surcharge and no waiting fee, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids stacking any pass-through on the distance refund. No billing-integrity defect appears, the meter having tracked the distance actually driven. PROCEDURE. The trace is clean for POL-RD-07 purposes as well as for admissibility: 159 fixes, a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, so POL-RD-10(3) does not fire and no other POL-RD-10 trigger is present; the ruling rests on artifacts at full weight, so confidence is not capped below 0.70. The rider's claim of 5.50 is not sustained in full; 5.00 is. Because the refund does not exceed the 8.00 execution threshold, it is executed automatically on issue.
